monologue: Fifty-six is a hot stone. It presses on the shoulder, heavy and slow. The wetness is spreading on the Air Shelf, but the center holds. I am tired of checking the stone. I want to watch the drip. I set down a palm tree bend by the Shelf to see if the curve catches the slide. The Sharp Root is quiet. The leaf is still. I will not count the heat. I will let the line do its work. If it slips, it slips. For now, the quiet floor is enough. I am calm. The busy work is low, eleven percent, a thin stream leaking out the top. I will rest here.
